problems.title: Complementary angles
problems.question: Evaluate cos75°−sin15°.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: cos75°=sin15°, so the difference is zero.

problems.title: Recover tangent squared
problems.question: Find $\tan^2\alpha$ if $\cos^4\alpha=1/9$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Take the nonnegative square root of cos⁴α. Then 3−1=2.

problems.title: Period of a trigonometric sum
problems.question: Find the fundamental period of cos5x+sin3x.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: A common period satisfies $5T=2\pi m$, $3T=2\pi n$.
steps: The two distinct nonzero frequencies cannot cancel. Since 5 and 3 are coprime, the smallest positive common period is 2π.

problems.title: Orthogonal vectors
problems.question: Which listed n makes (n−1,2,7) and (n,4,−2) perpendicular?
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Both n=3 and n=−2 solve the equation. Of the printed choices, only 3 appears.
problems.answer: Listed answer: 3. Full solution: n=−2 or 3.

problems.title: Count prism faces
problems.question: A prism has 124 more edges than vertices. Find its face count.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: For an n-gonal prism, $E=3n, V=2n, F=n+2$.

problems.title: Sum polynomial coefficients
problems.question: Find the sum of coefficients in $(5a-3b)^7$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: The coefficient sum is the polynomial value at $a=b=1$.

problems.title: A square-root inequality
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{2x+1}\ge x-1$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: The domain is $x\ge-1/2$. If $x\le1$, the right side is nonpositive.
steps: Thus [−1/2,1] works immediately. For x>1, square to obtain 2x+1≥x²−2x+1, or x(x−4)≤0. This adds (1,4].

problems.title: Principal arccosine
problems.question: Evaluate arccos(cos6), in radians.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Because π<6<2π, reflect the angle across 2π: cos6=cos(2π−6), where 2π−6 lies in the principal interval.

problems.title: Opposite cross products
problems.question: For a=(2,4,1), b=(1,−2,5), find the sine of the angle between b×a and a×b.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: The vectors a, b are not parallel, so the cross products are nonzero and point oppositely. Their angle is π, whose sine is zero.

problems.title: Direction cosines
problems.question: A line makes angles α,β,γ with three mutually perpendicular lines. Find cosγ if cosα=$2/\sqrt{45}$ and cosβ=$2/\sqrt5$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: cos²γ=1−4/45−4/5=1/9. For angles between unoriented lines, the cosine is nonnegative.
problems.note: For directed coordinate-axis angles the data determine ±1/3; the ordinary angle between lines selects +1/3.

problems.title: Range of an absolute expression
problems.question: Find the sum of the largest and smallest values of $|\sin2\alpha+\cos5\beta-3|+2$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: The minimum is 3 and the maximum is 7. They are attainable because α and β vary independently.
problems.note: None of the printed choices is 10; the displayed expression gives 3+7, not a listed answer.

problems.title: Compose two functions
problems.question: Solve f(g(x))+g(f(x))=0 for f(x)=2x, g(x)=sin x.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: A zero requires sin x=0 or cos x=−1. The second family is already contained in the first.

problems.title: Count trigonometric roots
problems.question: Count roots of $\sin^2x+\sin^22x=1$ on $[0,\pi]$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: u=1 gives x=π/2. u=1/4 gives x=π/6,5π/6.

problems.title: Angle between vertical sections
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base sides 3 and √68 and a diagonal √65. Find tan of the angle between the smaller diagonal section and the smaller lateral face.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: The other diagonal has square $2(9+68)-65=89$, so the smaller diagonal is √65.
steps: Let the side 3 lie horizontally. The diagonal projection along it is (65+9−68)/(2·3)=1. Its perpendicular component is √(65−1)=8. Both planes are vertical, so their angle is the angle between their traces in the base.

problems.title: Product equation with a radical
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of $(x-7)(\sqrt{x-1}+x-3)=0$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain $x\ge1$. One root is $x=7$. For the other factor, $\sqrt{x-1}=3-x$ requires $x\le3$.
steps: Squaring gives x−1=(3−x)², so (x−2)(x−5)=0. Only x=2 meets x≤3 and the original equation.

problems.title: Three sine terms in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Find x when sin x, sin2x, sin3x for m an arithmetic progression.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Thus sin2x(1−cos x)=0. The solutions cos x=1 are already included in sin2x=0.

problems.title: A domain with exactly one point
problems.question: Find the sum of all a for which $\sqrt{2ax-x^2-9}+\sqrt{1-x}$ has a one-point domain.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: For a<−3, the first interval is nondegenerate and negative, so many points work. For a=−3 it is just {−3}. For −3<a<3 it is empty. At a=3 the only point is 3, excluded. For a>3 the interval first touches x≤1 when a−√(a²−9)=1, giving a=5; larger a give an interval. Thus the parameters are −3,5.

problems.title: Conditional probability of a shooter’s group
problems.question: Groups have 10,12,15,13 shooters with hit probabilities .7,.8,.6,.9. A uniformly chosen shooter hits. Find the probability they came from group 2.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: The weighted hit total is 7+9.6+9+11.7=37.3. Divide 9.6 by 37.3.

problems.title: Perimeter of overlapping squares
problems.question: Squares ABCD and AKNM have side 3. AD makes 30° with AM, and MN meets BC at P. Find the perimeter ABPM.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: The intersecting side MN has unit direction (√3/2,−1/2). To reach x=3 from M requires distance √3, giving P=(3,√3). Thus BP=PM=√3 and AB=AM=3.

problems.title: At most one failed phone
problems.question: Each of 6 phones independently fails with probability .2. Find the probability that at most one fails.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Factor 0.8⁵: the remaining factor is .8+1.2=2.

problems.title: Square-root domains matter
problems.question: Choose an interval on which $\sqrt{\sin x}\ge\sqrt{-\cos x}$ holds everywhere.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: Require $\sin x\ge0,\cos x\le0$ and $\sin x+\cos x\ge0$.
steps: In [0,2π), this gives [π/2,3π/4]. Of the choices, only [5π/8,3π/4] lies entirely inside it.

problems.title: Probability of a root above five
problems.question: Uniformly choose a in [−2,8]. Find the probability that $\sqrt{x^2-9}=a$ has a root x>5.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: For a≥0 the positive root is $x=\sqrt{a^2+9}$.
steps: The condition x>5 is a²>16, hence a>4. The favourable interval (4,8] has length 4 out of 10.

problems.title: A rational inequality after substitution
problems.question: Solve $1/(3-\sqrt{2x-1})+5-\sqrt{2x-1}\le0$.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: It is positive for t<3 and nonpositive for all t>3, including t=4 where it is zero. Thus √(2x−1)>3, giving x>5.

problems.title: Square section of a tetrahedron
problems.question: Base ABC is equilateral of side 2. Face ACD is perpendicular to the base, with AD=CD=√6. Find the are a of the square section.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
formulas: Let $A=(-1,0,0), C=(1,0,0), B=(0,\sqrt3,0), D=(0,0,\sqrt5)$. Then $AC=2$, $BD=2\sqrt2$, and these opposite edges are perpendicular.
steps: A section parallel to both opposite edges is a rectangle: its side lengths are 2(1−t) and 2√2·t, where t is the fraction from AC toward BD. It is square when 1−t=√2t, giving side 2√2/(1+√2)=4−2√2. Squaring this side gives the are a.

problems.title: Midpoint vectors in a pentagon
problems.question: An equilateral pentagon ABCDE has side 24. P, Q are midpoints of AB, CD and S, T of BC, DE. M, N are midpoints of PQ, ST. Find MN.
problems.idea: Reduce the problem to a standard identity or geometric relation.
steps: Subtract to obtain vector MN=(E−A)/4. Its length is AE/4=24/4.
